- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to counteract pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap downward revisions to avoid excessive lag.  
- If forecast mean is > 80 and true outcome is consistently below 75, apply mean reversion bias: subtract 2–4% from forecast if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture early downward momentum; if sentiment turns negative within 5 days, reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., +0.33, -0.33, +0.33), model tends to lag; apply a 1–2% lag correction to forecast for next period.
